survey: A gold three-arm candelabra seen from the front, slightly from above. A round, domed base sits flat at the bottom. A turned stem with two knops rises from it to a central collar. Two U-shaped arms leave that collar, one on each side, curve down and back up, and end in drip-pan cups with flanged rims. The central stem continues up to a third, slightly higher cup. Each cup holds a cream pillar candle that sits down inside the rim. Each candle has a short dark wick with one teardrop flame on it. The two arms mirror each other in shape, thickness and cup height. The object stands on its base against a plain background with no surface, which is normal for a card. Every part joins solidly: the arms meet the stem at the collar, the candles sit in their cups, and the flames sit on the wicks. The weight is balanced over the base, the count of three arms and three candles is consistent, and nothing floats or passes through anything else.
